title: Automate Opus Clip: A Beginner Setup Guide (2026)
summary: Automate Opus Clip using import, scheduling, and API access to convert long videos into short, publishable clips with no manual work between steps.
body_markdown:
## Send clips via scheduler or API


Once the clip set is stable, you send it out through Opus Clip's own scheduler or its API, and your plan decides which of the two you get.


I have no verified Free, Starter and Pro comparison of scheduler, API access, platforms and seats, so no plan table is printed here.


Read those rows on Opus Clip's pricing page, and treat the scheduler and the API as plan-gated until you've seen them listed for yours.


Plan around these caps, which are quoted from Opus Clip's Help Center and should be rechecked there before you build.


Help says YouTube and TikTok allow 15 posts a day each and Instagram 40, so **YouTube and TikTok become your bottleneck** if you're posting across all platforms.


However fast you generate clips, a batch of 20 bound for YouTube takes two days to clear.


### Connect accounts and schedule from the dashboard


Connect each social account once in the dashboard, then queue clips against a posting time. Length matters here because the platforms differ.


Per RevID's platform-limits chart, a third-party comparison rather than Opus Clip's own documentation, **YouTube Shorts tops out at 3 minutes** , Instagram Reels at 20 minutes, and TikTok on the web at 60 minutes.


That means you'll need to edit content differently for each platform when cross-posting.


A clip cut for Shorts fits everywhere. A clip cut to fill TikTok's allowance fits nowhere else, so set your template's maximum length to the shortest platform you post to.


### Request API access and make the first call


Before building on the API, check the API column, because access depends on your plan. If your tier doesn't include it, you have two options: upgrade, or stay in the dashboard and download finished clips in batches for the next stage.


> A clip cut for Shorts fits everywhere. A clip cut to fill TikTok's allowance fits nowhere else, so set your template's maximum length to the shortest platform you post to.


If your plan includes it, request a key from your account settings and take the endpoints, auth header and request fields from Opus Clip's current API documentation, since they change. Don't copy them from a tutorial.


Make your first call the simplest one the docs list, using the key Opus Clip gave you.


### Poll Opus Clip or use a webhook


Because clip generation takes time, your code has to find out when a project is done. If the docs list a webhook, use it, because it costs no requests.


If you can only poll, do the arithmetic against the 30 requests a minute limit, per Help.


6 requests a minute is what one project checked every 10 seconds uses, so five projects running at once use the entire allowance.


Poll every 30 seconds or longer, which means detection can lag up to 30 seconds behind actual completion, and stop polling a project once it reports complete.
